_note: Hand-written examples (not taken from OWASP Benchmark, to avoid leaking answers). Keyed by CWE id; triage_llm.py --fewshot adds the matching entries to the prompt.

89.why: Request parameter is concatenated into the SQL string.
The value is bound as a parameter; the query text is constant.

78.code:
String host = req.getParameter("host");
Runtime.getRuntime().exec("sh -c ping " + host);
78.why: Attacker-controlled text reaches a shell command.
The tainted value is overwritten by a constant before the sink.

22.code:
String name = req.getParameter("f");
new FileInputStream(new File(BASE_DIR, name));
22.why: Request data chooses the file path; '../' can escape BASE_DIR.
The value used is the constant stored under key 'b', not the request data.

79.code:
String q = req.getParameter("q");
resp.getWriter().println("Results for " + q);
79.why: Request data is written to the HTML response without encoding.
The value is HTML-encoded for this output context.
